Vivek Ramaswamy kicked off a bus tour this weekend with other members of the
Ohio Republican ticket, at the height of a political firestorm over the
"[shameful](https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6164220-nancy-mace-vivek-
ramaswamy-political-ad/)" and [uniquely revolting ad
campaign](https://zeteo.com/p/the-ugliest-midterms-race-just-got) he launched
against his Democratic opponent for governor.

Now, as a result of that ad campaign, businesses are having second thoughts
about hosting the Republican politicians if Ramaswamy is there, **Zeteo** has
learned.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

"We're getting calls that people don't want him there," a top Ohio Republican
tells us. This source adds that some business owners and event hosts have
explicitly told them that they do not want the horrendous publicity - or angry
phone calls, or social-media attacks, or customer complaints - that they would
get for hosting Ramaswamy's campaign tour at this juncture.
